description: Major legends, lost vessels, cursed regions, and forgotten civilizations from the final source section.

entries.title: The Dwarven Lecture on Airflight
entries.summary: A traditional Dwarven account explains flight through stonecraft, runes, pressure, engineering discipline, and distrust of elegant shortcuts.
body: The lecture frames Dwarven airflight as the controlled persuasion of heavy material rather than effortless levitation. Reliable lift emerges from runes, reinforced stone, steam, careful maintenance, and engineers who respect load and failure.
Its humorous and argumentative tone also expresses cultural pride: a Dwarven vessel should endure damage, remain repairable, and never depend on beauty alone.

entries.title: Aelric Skywarden
entries.summary: Aelric is remembered as the first protector of the light and an exemplar of the Sky Warden calling.
body: Aelric's legend presents protection as an active duty carried into dangerous skies rather than a title granted by a temple. His example joins divine purpose, aerial travel, courage, and defense of vulnerable communities.
Later Sky Wardens use the story to explain why their order stands between settlements and the darkness beyond safe routes.

entries.title: Captain Daeron Ironheart Veld
entries.summary: A captain's sacrifice during the Battle of the Shattered Skies became the foundation of Kaysender's neutral-ground symbol and compact.
body: Daeron Veld is remembered for placing common survival above factional victory during a catastrophic aerial battle. His conduct transformed the wheel and Ouroboros into a promise that enemies could meet, bargain, and shelter without immediate betrayal.
The story is invoked wherever the [[neutral-ground-network|neutral-ground mark]] appears, though factions disagree over how faithfully modern establishments follow his ideals.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Origin of the Neutral Ground Symbol

entries.title: The Lost Tomb of Captain Veld
entries.summary: A storm-hidden island may hold Captain Veld's tomb, his wheel, and artifacts capable of guiding ships through tempests.
body: The island appears only during the fiercest storms, when sailors report a silhouette, ghostly crew, and fragmentary routes through the clouds. Incomplete maps circulate among treasure hunters, imperial agents, and the Black Fleet.

Expeditions vanish or return disoriented, claiming that the weather itself rejected them. The tomb may reward worthy seekers, protect itself from greed, or be a legend constructed around Veld's sacrifice.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: The Lost Tomb of Captain Daeron Veld

entries.title: The Ashen Phoenix
entries.summary: A treasure-laden ghost ship of the old Draconic Armada drifts near the northern coasts, always visible and never quite reachable.
body: The Ashen Phoenix was an immense obsidian and gilded-scale vessel carrying Dragon Lord Vraxion's hoard during a war among the skies. Its crew died, its fleet was broken, and the ship disappeared from official history.

Recent witnesses describe tattered black sails, a faint ember glow, voices in fog, and coins rolling across an empty deck. Pirates and bounty hunters pursue it despite warnings that its treasure is an illusion or curse.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Ghost Ship of the Draconic Armada: The Ashen Phoenix

entries.title: The Frozen Glaciers and Cursed Airways
entries.summary: Floating northern glaciers form a shifting maze of ice, storms, frozen mist, wrecks, and voices of the lost.
body: The glaciers are said to be the prison of an ancient civilization that bargained with sky spirits for command of frost and wind, then demanded too much. Their cities vanished as living ice and jagged spires closed around them.

The Cursed Airways change direction, trap hulls, tear sails, and conceal routes in freezing mist. Ships entering the maze may emerge years later, drift forever, or join the voices heard on calm nights.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Frozen Glaciers and the Cursed Airways

entries.title: The Undead Acropolis
entries.summary: A ruined city beyond the Frozen Glaciers is guarded by intelligent undead air sailors and three eternal captains.
body: The Acropolis hangs in the frozen north, its inhabitants bound as skeletons and wraiths rather than allowed to pass on. Bone, ice, and shadow ships patrol the surrounding airways and can manipulate wind, storm, and frost.
Three artifact-bearing captains command the fleet. They pursue intruders through a labyrinth of ice and dark magic, and survivors often return unable to explain how they escaped.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: The Undead Acropolis and Watchers of the Frozen Skies

entries.title: Azh'Thanar, the Unbroken Continent
entries.summary: A lost western continent holds primeval beasts, impossible giant-built ruins, and records deliberately buried by elves, dwarves, and dragons.
body: Azh'Thanar is described as a surviving continent of vast jungles, immense rivers, towering mountains, giant reptiles, and woolly titans. Its structures were built on a scale large enough for dragons or greater beings.

Banquet-hall skulls, bridge-like spines, and colossal doors suggest a civilization predating known nations and perhaps the Shattering. Elven accounts vanished, Dwarven records were sealed, and ancient dragons refuse to discuss what once lived there.
